_readme: Tea catalog. Each entry: name, type (green | black | oolong | white | puerh | herbal), origin, flavors (pick from: grassy, floral, malty, smoky, citrus, stone fruit, spiced, earthy, nutty, mineral, vegetal, creamy), intensity 1-5 (how assertive the cup is), caffeine (none | low | medium | high), astringency 1-5 (how drying and tannic), brew { water, steep, leaf }, and a one-sentence description of the cup. Add a tea by copying any entry and editing it.

teas.name: Sencha
teas.description: Bright and grassy, with a savory, steamed-greens edge and a brisk, slightly bitter finish.

teas.name: Gyokuro

brew.leaf: 2 tsp (5 g) in a small cup of water

teas.description: Thick, brothy, and intensely savory, like a sweet seaweed broth with almost no bitterness.

teas.name: Matcha

brew.leaf: 1 tsp (2 g) powder in 70 ml water

teas.description: Dense and vivid green, savory and sweet at once, with a velvety body and a lingering bittersweet edge.

teas.name: Genmaicha
teas.description: Toasted rice gives it a warm, popcorn-like nuttiness over a light, grassy green tea base.

teas.name: Hojicha
teas.description: Roasty and mellow, with toasted-grain and caramel notes and almost no bitterness.

teas.name: Kukicha
teas.description: Light, sweet, and creamy, with a gentle nutty-vegetal flavor from the twigs and stems it is made from.

teas.name: Dragon Well (Longjing)
teas.description: Pan-fired and flat-leafed, tasting of toasted chestnut and sweet snap peas with a smooth finish.

teas.name: Gunpowder Green
teas.description: Rolled into tight pellets, it brews a bold, faintly smoky green with a firm, drying grip.

teas.name: Jasmine Pearls
teas.description: Hand-rolled green tea scented with fresh jasmine blossoms — perfumed, sweet, and smooth.

teas.name: Assam
teas.description: Brisk, full-bodied, and deeply malty — the backbone of most breakfast blends, and happy with milk.

teas.name: Darjeeling First Flush
teas.description: Pale gold and lively, with fresh floral and green-grape notes and a crisp, slightly drying finish.

teas.name: Keemun
teas.description: Smooth and gently winey, with dried-plum fruit, a hint of cocoa, and a faint wisp of smoke.

teas.name: Lapsang Souchong
teas.description: Smoked over pinewood fires, it tastes like a campfire — resinous and savory, with a dried-fruit sweetness underneath.

teas.name: Ceylon
teas.description: Bright, brisk, and coppery, with a lively citrus edge that also makes it a great iced tea.

teas.name: Yunnan Dian Hong
teas.description: Golden-tipped and plush, with malty sweet-potato and cocoa notes and very little bite.

teas.name: English Breakfast
teas.origin: Blend of Assam, Ceylon, and Kenyan teas

brew.leaf: 1 tsp (2.5 g) or one bag per cup

teas.description: A sturdy, brisk blend — malty, round, and built to take milk.

teas.name: Earl Grey
teas.description: Black tea perfumed with bergamot oil — fragrant and citrusy over a brisk, clean base.

teas.name: Masala Chai

brew.water: Simmer in half water, half milk
brew.leaf: 1 tbsp (5 g) spiced blend per cup

teas.description: Strong black tea simmered with cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, and clove — sweet-spiced and rich with milk.

teas.name: Tieguanyin
teas.description: Orchid-like and buttery, with a lilac perfume and a sweet, lingering finish.

teas.name: Jin Xuan Milk Oolong
teas.description: Soft and naturally creamy, with a sweet-milk, buttery texture and a light floral lift.

teas.name: Alishan High Mountain Oolong
teas.description: Light and lush, with a sweet floral fragrance, a creamy body, and a clean, mineral finish from high-altitude gardens.

teas.name: Dong Ding
teas.description: Medium-roasted and honeyed, balancing toasted-nut warmth with a soft floral sweetness.

teas.name: Oriental Beauty
teas.description: Honey-sweet and fruity, with ripe peach and muscatel notes and a smooth, rounded body.

teas.name: Da Hong Pao
teas.description: Roasted and rocky, with a deep mineral backbone, charred-nut warmth, and a ripe stone-fruit sweetness.

teas.name: Phoenix Dan Cong (Mi Lan Xiang)

brew.steep: 2 minutes — it turns bitter if pushed

teas.description: Intensely aromatic, with honey-orchid perfume, ripe apricot-and-lychee fruit, and a sharp, lingering finish.

teas.name: Silver Needle (Bai Hao Yin Zhen)

brew.leaf: 2 tbsp (3 g) per cup — the buds are fluffy

teas.description: Made only from downy buds, it is pale, silky, and subtle — hay, honeydew melon, and a whisper of flowers.

teas.name: White Peony (Bai Mu Dan)
teas.description: Fuller than Silver Needle, with a fresh, hay-like sweetness, soft floral notes, and a gentle melon finish.

teas.name: Shou Mei
teas.description: Darker and more robust than other whites, with woody, autumn-leaf depth and a dried-apricot sweetness.

teas.name: Ripe Pu-erh (Shou)

brew.steep: Rinse for 10 seconds, then steep 3 minutes

teas.description: Dark, smooth, and deeply earthy, like forest floor and dark cocoa, with almost no astringency.

teas.name: Raw Pu-erh (Young Sheng)

brew.steep: Rinse for 10 seconds, then steep 1–2 minutes

teas.description: Sharp and bittersweet, with a strong vegetal bite, an apricot-like sweetness behind it, and plenty of grip.

teas.name: Chrysanthemum Pu-erh (Ju Pu)

brew.steep: Rinse for 10 seconds, then steep 3 minutes
brew.leaf: 1 tsp (3 g) pu-erh plus 3–4 dried flowers per cup

teas.description: Earthy ripe pu-erh brewed with whole chrysanthemum flowers, which lift it with a honeyed floral brightness.

teas.name: Chamomile

brew.leaf: 1 tbsp (2 g) dried flowers per cup

teas.description: Soft and honeyed, with the apple-like sweetness of whole chamomile flowers.

teas.name: Rooibos
teas.description: Naturally sweet and woody, with honey and vanilla notes and a round, smooth body.

teas.name: Rooibos Chai
teas.origin: Rooibos with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and clove

brew.steep: 6 minutes, then add warm milk if you like

teas.description: All the cinnamon-and-cardamom warmth of chai over sweet, woody rooibos, with no tea leaves at all.

teas.name: Honeybush
teas.origin: Eastern and Western Cape, South Africa
teas.description: Like a lighter, more floral rooibos, with honeyed sweetness and a dried-apricot note.

teas.name: Hibiscus

brew.leaf: 1 tsp (2 g) dried petals per cup

teas.description: Deep ruby and sharply tart, like cranberry with a squeeze of lime, bright enough to make you pucker.

teas.name: Ginger

brew.leaf: 1 tsp (2 g) dried root, or 4 thin slices fresh, per cup

teas.description: Peppery and hot, with a clean, lemony bite that builds as it steeps.

teas.name: Lemongrass

brew.leaf: 1 tbsp (2 g) cut lemongrass per cup

teas.description: Light, sweet, and lemony, with a fresh grassy edge and none of the sourness of actual lemon.

teas.name: Roasted Barley Tea (Mugicha)

brew.leaf: 1 tbsp (8 g) roasted barley per cup

teas.description: Toasty and grain-sweet, a bit like dark toast or coffee without any of the bitterness.

teas.name: Yerba Mate
teas.description: Herbaceous and bitter-edged, with a grassy, tobacco-like depth and a long, drying finish.
